clue.text: Adult female briefly aroused and consumed with emotion

indicators.note: something put briefly is cut short, so the word loses its final letter
to be aroused is to be stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: A grown woman, quickly excited, is overcome by her feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female' is not the usual abbreviation F here: shorn of its last letter, FEMAL is rearranged after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aflame is burning, figuratively ablaze with passion or strong feeling.

clue.text: Breaks FBI agents implicated by fellow informers

indicators.note: implicated means folded in or entangled, so the agents sit inside the informers

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
a rat is one who betrays others to the authorities
G-men are US federal agents

explanation.surface: Federal agents' cover is blown by colleagues who tip off others.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragments are bits broken off something, the pieces left by breaks.

clue.text: Iron horse's pulling power?

blocks.note: surface reading: the hauling strength of a steam locomotive, nicknamed the iron horse
setter's reading: the attraction an iron-bearing beast would exert, as a magnet does

explanation.walkthrough: Pulling power for a person means charisma; for a creature made of iron it would be literal magnetic attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means personal charm or charisma, and also once meant hypnotic mesmerism; here literal magnetic pull.

clue.text: Former Chancellor of the Exchequer accepting America's apology

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the country's abbreviation goes inside

blocks.note: ex means former
the initials of the title, with Exchequer standing for its E
US is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: An ex-Chancellor of the Exchequer accepting an American apology.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is Britain's finance minister.
explanation.definitionFit: An excuse is a justification or plea offered to defend oneself, a kind of apology.

clue.text: Instrument failing to maintain charged particle's congruent state

indicators.note: failing to keep hold of something means it is lost, so those letters drop out of the instrument

blocks.note: a squeezebox instrument
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A meter that can't hold a charge is no longer in a consistent state.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'particle's' is the possessive linking it to the definition: the instrument without the ion is the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in accord means agreeing or matching, a state of harmony or congruence.

clue.text: Oral record supporting two articles in parallel

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so what counts is the sound of the word
in a down entry, supporting means sitting underneath the other pieces

blocks.note: the indefinite articles an and a
a log is a record such as a ship's journal

explanation.surface: A spoken recording backing up a pair of essays published side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: An analogue is something comparable or corresponding to another thing, a parallel.

clue.text: Relations based on physical chemistry?

blocks.note: surface reading: links between branches of science, physical chemistry being one discipline
setter's reading: sexual relations based on bodily attraction, the knowledge being physical

explanation.walkthrough: Physical chemistry is a real science subject, but 'chemistry' between people is attraction and 'relations' is a euphemism for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a legal and biblical euphemism for sexual intercourse.

clue.text: Upgrade level for those attending

indicators.note: those attending are an audience listening, so the word is judged by ear

blocks.note: to raze is to level a building to the ground

explanation.surface: Improving the standard offered to people who turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift or promote it to a higher grade.

clue.text: Talked about limits of convergence in empty space

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters are kept
in places those letters inside the space

blocks.note: a void is an empty space
its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A lecture on where lines meet in a vacuum.
explanation.definitionFit: Voiced means expressed aloud in words, so spoke or talked about.

clue.text: Delayed dates rearranged around start of year

indicators.note: rearranged means put in a new order, so the letters are reordered
the start of a word is its first letter
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the single letter

blocks.note: anagram fodder
first letter

explanation.surface: Postponed appointments are reshuffled at the turn of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay something, such as an execution, is to postpone or halt it, so stayed means delayed.

clue.text: National borders ignored by EU country

indicators.note: ignoring the borders of a word means leaving off its first and last letters

blocks.note: Romania is a member state of the European Union

explanation.surface: A citizen whose frontiers are disregarded by a European Union member.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani is a citizen of Oman, so a national of that Gulf country.

clue.text: Champion rescue mission and support for people in Peak District?

definitions.text: support for people in Peak District?

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for champion
evacuation of people by aircraft

explanation.surface: A champion, a rescue operation and backing for hikers in a Derbyshire national park.
explanation.walkthrough: The Peak District is a hilly national park in northern England; the question mark marks the pun on 'peak' as mountain top.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairlift carries skiers or walkers up a mountainside, holding them up on the way to the peaks.

clue.text: Rage at pretty nurses with pity

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold in the arms, so one word cradles the other inside it

blocks.note: a passion is a fit of anger
taken as written
comely means attractive

explanation.surface: Fury at a good-looking nurse, combined with sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty nurses' reads as attractive nursing staff; in fact 'nurses' is a verb, with COMELY holding PASSION and AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To act compassionately is to act out of sympathy and mercy, that is, with pity.

clue.text: Mover and shaker upset many in party

indicators.note: in a down-facing image, upset means turned over, so the word is read backwards
in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An influential figure has upset many people at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is an energetic, forceful person who gets things moving, a mover and shaker.

clue.text: Keep off the grass and other plants

blocks.note: to duck is to dodge or avoid
weed and grass are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A park sign warning people off the lawn and the flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep off the grass' reads as a single notice, but it splits into avoid plus cannabis; 'other' acknowledges that weed is itself a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Duckweed is a tiny floating pond plant, growing in masses that cover the water surface.

clue.text: Foreigner making a point he and I misconstrued

indicators.note: something misconstrued is wrongly put together, so the letters come out in another order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: An outsider argues a point that two people have misunderstood.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ethiopian, from Ethiopia, is a foreigner to a British setter; the definition is broad by example.

clue.text: Win female author will refuse

definitions.note: a noun, rubbish, not the verb

blocks.note: to land a prize is to win it
F is the abbreviation for female
the writer saying 'I will' is I'll

explanation.surface: A woman writer who wins a prize says she will turn it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun, stressed on the first syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Landfill is waste buried in the ground, and also the rubbish itself.

clue.text: Student class finishing early following picket

indicators.note: finishing early means stopping before the end, so the last letter is lost
following means coming after, so one piece is placed behind the other

blocks.note: a picket is a pointed post or stake
a grade is a class or rank

explanation.surface: A student group leaving lessons early to join a picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picket' suggests strikers, but it is the wooden stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A postgrad, short for postgraduate, is a student working beyond a first degree.

clue.text: Bird recorded Kind of Blue

indicators.note: a recording is something heard played back, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

blocks.note: the petrel is a seabird

explanation.surface: Charlie Parker, known as Bird, recorded Miles Davis's album Kind of Blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Kind of Blue is a Miles Davis jazz album, and Bird is Charlie Parker's nickname; both are decoys.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrol blue is a deep greenish-blue shade, so petrol is a kind of blue.

clue.text: Behave protectively towards different male leads

indicators.note: leads means goes in front, so the abbreviation is placed before the other word

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
other means different

explanation.surface: Guarding something as various men take the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To mother someone is to care for and shield them as a parent would.

clue.text: Engineers offend, leaving in consequence

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the following short word goes out of the verb

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to insult is to offend
taken as written; this is what goes

explanation.surface: Engineers give offence and walk out as a consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is the pair of letters taken away; the final 'in' only joins the wordplay to the definition. RE is the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A result is an outcome, what follows as a consequence of something.

clue.text: He may have fled corrupt regime?

definitions.text: He may have fled corrupt regime?

indicators.note: corrupt means debased or spoiled, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A man who may have escaped from a crooked government.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay at once: the exile is literally a rearranged regime.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigré is someone who has left their own country, often for political reasons.

clue.text: Scruffy people treated badly by African country in large number

indicators.note: done badly means done wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order
in places the preceding words inside the number

blocks.note: anagram fodder
Mali is a West African country
tons means lots

explanation.surface: Ragged people mistreated in great numbers by an African state.
explanation.definitionFit: A tatterdemalion is an old word for a person in tattered clothes, a ragamuffin.

clue.text: Part of statutory role for academic staff

indicators.note: part of means a piece lies inside the next word, so the letters are taken from within it

blocks.note: letters within the word

explanation.surface: Part of a legally required duty for university staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a tutor, teaching small groups, is one of the jobs academic staff do.

clue.text: Lasting longer than Open University tutor's primary source of income

indicators.note: primary means first, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: OU is the abbreviation for the Open University, Britain's distance-learning university
opening letter
one's living is how one earns money

explanation.surface: A distance-learning tutor's main earnings outlasting something.
explanation.definitionFit: Outliving someone means surviving them, staying alive longer.

clue.text: Training exercise is not well introduced by doctor

indicators.note: introduced by means preceded by, so the doctor's abbreviation goes first

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A doctor brings in an exercise regime for an unwell patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a repeated practice routine, as in fire drill or military drill.

clue.text: Border controlled by China is most important

indicators.note: something controlled is held in check, so one word is held within the other

blocks.note: china means friend in Cockney rhyming slang (china plate, mate)
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A frontier policed by Beijing is a top priority.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C on China suggests the country; it is the slang for a mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal means primary or fundamental, of first importance.

clue.text: Leave like Britain, not without heart

indicators.note: without its heart a word loses its middle letter

blocks.note: since Brexit, Britain is a former member of the European Union
taken as written, before losing its centre

explanation.surface: A wry nod to Brexit: Britain leaving, and not half-heartedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' recalls the Brexit campaign; here it is the plural verb in a stage direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt is the Latin stage direction meaning they go off, so actors leave the stage.
